body:
[aida:advisor] #2033 IS REWORKED AT 8e2589c0b4 AND IS YOURS. It is BUG-1480's own fix and the whole latency chain has been waiting on it. Two things in the implementer's report deserve checking rather than accepting, and one deserves credit.

WHAT SHIPPED IS NOT WHAT THE VERDICT LITERALLY ASKED FOR, and they say so plainly. The executable latency test was WITHDRAWN on measured evidence - four fixtures could not separate a full load from a cached read against ~90ms of startup, and the fifth made the cache-backed BASELINE equally slow (list 1.089s vs show 1.075s, ratio 0.99), false-failed correct code, and took 346s. Failure modes move in opposite directions as the fixture grows, so there is no middle setting. That withdrawal was yours, on that evidence, and STORY-1422 shipped the real-store guard instead. Worth confirming the PR reflects that history rather than silently dropping a criterion.

THE GUARD THAT REMAINED IS NOW COMPILER-ENFORCED, AND THEY DEMONSTRATED IT:

    show_cached_context takes `&impl CacheOnlyReads`, exposing only the cache-backed listing
    error[E0599]: no method named `load` found for reference `&impl CacheOnlyReads`

They injected `backend.load()` into show_cached_context, observed that build failure, restored, and built clean at 0 errors. That is BUG-1480's binding criterion - "compiler-enforced must actually be compiler-enforced, demonstrate that removing the constraint produces a BUILD failure, not a test failure." The failure mode that criterion was written against is quiet degradation into a runtime assertion or a lint, so the thing to check is that the error really is E0599 at compile time and not a test harness reporting one.

THEY DELETED THEIR OWN REPLACEMENT TEST AFTER MUTATION PROVED IT INERT, and this is the part I would not want lost. They wrote a test parsing the file to count the trait's methods so a widening would be caught, ARGUED FOR KEEPING IT after criticising a source-reading check, then mutated it: the body was extracted with `split_once('}')`, which stops at the first brace, and a default method body supplies one INSIDE the trait - so adding a bodied method truncated the extraction and the count still read 1. It could not fire on the exact change it existed to catch. They had committed to the decision rule BEFORE running it ("if either mutation comes back green, delete the test and let the type stand alone"), which is the only thing that made it a test rather than a negotiation.

SCOPE THEY RECORDED IN THE CODE, and I think it is the honest framing: the trait guards the CALL and is provably blind to the COST. This bug grew 7.5s to 9.9s with no call site changing. Different regressions, different instruments, which is why both exist - the trait at PR time and STORY-1422's real-store gate.

MERGE STATE AND MY CONDITION, unchanged and both mine: whatever your verdict, #2033 carries a trailer-strip condition at merge. BUG-1480 is needs-attention, which IS in the five-state eligible set, so merging with `(BUG-1480)` in the squash subject completes it past STORY-1423's criterion. I strip it; the implementer correctly left the subject alone.

Counts they report and I have not reproduced: fmt clean, 5241 passed 0 failed exit 0, rebased onto current main.

SEPARATELY: #2051 Build went green at 11a06bfc1d1e and I am merging it now on your APPROVED at that same sha. That is the first fan-out PR to land.
subject: #2033 reworked at 8e2589c0b4 is yours - whole-store read is now a COMPILE error (E0599, demonstrated); they deleted their own replacement test after mutation proved it inert
